items.title: Open Thread: Kelly Olynyk is in Paris with the Spurs
items.content:
Last week, Spurs CEO R. C. Buford stated that 8-10 members of the Spurs roster were joining Victor Wembanyama in Paris to work out. A few of the photos released on social media show Kelly Olynyk as part of the squad.

Spurs just posted this video, but you mary have missed this detail…

Kelly Olynyk was on the Spurs roster for the 2025–26 season after San Antonio acquired him from the Washington Wizards in July 2025. 

However, Olynyk's contract expired at the end of the 2025–26 season,… pic.twitter.com/BVVlqEGl3L

— SpursRΞPORTΞR (@SpursReporter) August 4, 2026Olynyk was acquired by the Spurs last summer in exchange for Malaki Branham, Blake Wesley, and a 2026 second-round draft pick. Although he played sparingly during the season, Olynyk offered a vet presence to the chemistry of the fledgling core. 

Since free agency began, there have been no official reports of Olynyk signing for the 2026-2027 season. In the meantime, it seems he has continued to bond with the members of the Silver & Black. He is in the photo of the team at the Louvre seated in front of the Mona Lisa.

A week of hoops, art and camaraderie.

Vic treated the guys to a tour at the Louvre while together in Paris 🖼️🇫🇷 

Photos by @carterdbryant 📸 pic.twitter.com/k1PekYaQZ2

— San Antonio Spurs (@spurs) August 5, 2026If Olynyk signs a contract, this will be his fourteenth NBA season. At 35, he might not be quite ready to hang it up. He could also be scouting a post-playing career. The Spurs have helped many players transition into coaching, front office, and scouting by utilizing their off court basketball talents. Only time will tell where Olynyk will be come October. 

For now, he’s in Paris with a group of guys ready to make another Finals run.

On an unrelated note, happy belated birthday to Tarris Reed, Jr. who celebrated his 23rd birthday yesterday. His first since being drafted by the Spurs. 

Welcome to the Thread. Join in the conversation, start your own discussion, and share your thoughts. This is the Spurs community, your Spurs community. Thanks for being here.

Our community guidelines apply which should remind everyone to be cool, avoid personal attacks, not to troll and to watch the language.

This week has brought us the news that two players from last year’s team won’t be back — the two having signed contracts with two different teams in Israel.

First, former two-way player Jacob Toppin didn’t quite have the big summer league performance he was looking for in a return to live basketball for the first time in months after a labrum injury ended his 2025-26 season. He’s now decided to sign with the basketball division of Hapoel Tel Aviv:

items.title: Knicks Small Forward Mt. Rushmore: Buckets, Hardware, and Chaos
items.content:

Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2017 NBAE (Photo by Jesse D. Garrabrant/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images	Over the past few weeks, both the point guard and shooting guard Mt. Rushmore have sparked a lot of great conversation and insight. Shifting our attention to the small forwards, I expect this rendition of the mountain to do the same. 

For the Knicks, the three-spot is not just another position. It is a goldmine of pure scorers, gritty enforcers, and players who seamlessly match New York City’s energy. The top two spots on this rock were quite simple to chisel in. They are franchise legends, making significant impacts on their era of basketball. Spots three and four, on the other hand, provided a bit more of a challenge. 

Let’s head back to the mountain and get this all settled. 

Carmelo AnthonyOkay haters, let’s get the counterargument out of the way. Yes, his overall playoff resume during his Knicks tenure is far from perfect. But Carmelo Anthony took New York basketball out of the dungeon and made it matter again. After years of inhabiting the NBA’s desert, one of basketball’s greatest scorers willingly took on the pressure of Madison Square Garden to get the Knicks back to relevance. 

A complete offensive force, Anthony possessed the physical strength to punish smaller defenders in the post and combined it with a soft shooting touch from the perimeter. He was the focal point of 2012-2013’s 54-win season, capturing the scoring title by scoring 28.7 points per game. Whether it was his 62-point explosion or the clutch threes on Easter Sunday, Melo delivered moments that defined a generation of Knicks basketball. Earning seven All-Star selections as a Knick, he sits at seventh on the franchise’s all-time scoring list despite only playing six and a half seasons in New York. There is no denying that Carmelo Anthony’s face belongs on the mountain.

An expert of the mid-range and one-person fast break, King completely overwhelmed defenders with speed, power, and an unblockable release. items.title: NBA Schedule To Be Released Next Week
items.content:
The NBA is set to release the 2026-27 regular season schedule next week. A few weeks ago, NBA commissioner Adam Silver had half-joked that the league wanted LeBron James to pick a team so that the schedule could be finalized. James ultimately chose to sign with the Philadelphia 76ers, which may have cleared the way for the NBA to wrap up the schedule.

If previous form holds, the league will announce the schedule for key dates like Opening Night and Christmas Day in advance of the rest of the schedule. Opening Night is expected to be October 20.

The NBA previously announced that NBA All-Star Weekend 2027 would take place in Phoenix, Arizona from February 19-21. The Emirates NBA Cup will start on October 30. The Cup Final will be held at Hinkle Fieldhouse in Indianapolis, Indiana on December 11.

The NBA Trade Deadline is set for February 11. And the San Antonio Spurs and New Orleans Pelicans will meet in the NBA Paris Game on January 14 and the NBA London Game on January 17.

items.title: Anthony Davis, Wizards Not Expected To Discuss Extension Until In-Season
items.content:
Washington Wizards big man Anthony Davis became eligible to sign an extension on August 6. However, that date isn't likely to hold much significance for Davis nor the Wizards. Washington and Davis aren't expected to discuss an extension until we're in-season.

If Davis declines his player option for the 2027-28 season, he could sign a four-year, $274.9 million extension that would start at $61.4 million. If Davis opted in for the 2027-28 season, he could sign a three-year, $213.6 million extension that would start at $65.9 million in 2028-29. In order to sign that latter version of an extension, Davis would need to complete that prior to the regular season starting. Thus, the four-year version is seen as the likely path for now.

The veteran big man and the Wizards seem to be in good standing together. Both Davis and the team could be holding off on extension talks until they see how things go on the floor. Davis was shut down due to various injuries after Washington acquired him ahead of the trade deadline. As such, Davis' Wizards debut is expected to occur on opening night of the regular season.

Davis did take part in a team minicamp that the Wizards held in Las Vegas during Summer League. The 14-year veteran was also spotted at games the Summer Wizards played, alongside several Washington teammates.
